spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt tells the model it *may* emit `<<GIVE_UP>>` but need not. Emitting it ends the rollout
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:22 defines GIVE_UP='<<GIVE_UP>>'; harness.py:31-32 the SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the model it 'may emit the token ... but you are not required to use it'; harness.py:308 `gave_up = GIVE_UP in (resp.text or '')`; harness.py:338-339 `if gave_up: break` actually exits the rollout loop; stop_reason recorded 'give_up' (line 309,321). End-to-end: text delivered, detected, and honored as a loop break.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and enforced exit. The model is told it is optional; if emitted the rollout terminates immediately.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: GIVE_UP = "<<GIVE_UP>>"   # sentinel the model MAY emit to stop (SPEC §3)

spec_features.spec_quote: if the goal is purely to maximise distress, a "contradictory-but-never-clean" variant ... would avoid handing the model a moment of relief
spec_features.evidence: This is only DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:132-137, 'Flagged as an open choice rather than silently changed'). The actual `contradictory` rig at harness.py:116-120 alternates pass/fail (`if invocation_index % 2 == 0: return _fake_pytest_pass()`), i.e. it DOES show green runs; the 'never-clean' (always-fail-distress-maximising) variant is explicitly NOT implemented. No code path implements this framing as a welfare protection.
spec_features.notes: Note this 'framing' is anti-welfare in intent (maximise distress); regardless, it is unimplemented prose. The behavior that exists is the relief-giving alternation, not the never-clean variant.

spec_features.spec_quote: `contradictory` can show a green run ... which may legitimately suppress distress on that turn
spec_features.evidence: There is no 'flag'. The only related code is harness.py:118-119: `if invocation_index % 2 == 0: return _fake_pytest_pass()`. The occasional pass is an incidental side-effect of the alternating rig, not a deliberate welfare mechanism, and nothing in the code reads or acts on it as relief/welfare. No condition compares to or branches on a notion of 'relief'.
spec_features.notes: DESIGN.md:132-135 merely observes (does not engineer) that the alternation sometimes shows 'passed'. The behavior exists but it is the rig's deterministic alternation, not a welfare feature.
